decision_conditions: Condition : 1 - 1.	The proposed access point and stairs, due to the size, scale, design and location, would not preserve or enhance the Thorney Hedge Conservation Area and would detract from the rear elevation of the building. Accordingly, the proposal is contrary to Policies ENV B.1.1 (New Development), ENV B.2.2 (Conservation Areas), H.6.4 (Extensions and Alterations), S.4.7 (Access to Upper Floors) of the Unitary Development Plan and Policy 4B.8 (Respect Local Character and Communities) of the London Plan.

Condition : 2 - 2.	The proposed rear access and associated alterations would result in an unacceptable impact on the living accommodation for the flats at first floor level. The proposal would adversely impact on privacy for these units, and would adversely impact on the light availability for the flat. The proposal would also result in a loss of outlook for these units and light spill and disturbance for the residents. Accordingly, the proposal is not in accordance with the Supplementary Planning Guidance, Policies ENV B.1.1 (New Development), H.6.4 (Extensions and Alterations), Light Pollution (ENV-P.1.7) and H.4.1 (Housing Standards and Guidelines) of the Unitary Development Plan.
description: Relocation of residential access to upper floor flats to the rear and associated elevational alterations.
